# FDG9100

> DO implement `IEnumerable<T>` on types implementing the Query Pattern.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.6.5 Supporting LINQ through the Query Pattern.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9100
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Implement IEnumerable<T> on '{0}', which declares the query method '{1}'

The text has no body. FDG9100 reports a class, struct or interface of any accessibility that declares an instance method of the Query Pattern of Figure 9-1 that takes a delegate (Where, Select, SelectMany, OrderBy, ThenBy, SkipWhile and Join, with OrderByDescending and ThenByDescending), with a parameter of a delegate type or of Expression<TDelegate> and a return value, and does not implement IEnumerable<T>; IQueryable<T> extends it and counts. A Query Pattern provided by extension methods, and the members of Figure 9-1 without a delegate (Union, Take, Skip, ElementAt), are not seen, so coverage is partial. Overrides and interface implementations are not reported, as they take their name from another member. Implementing an interface adds to the public API without changing a signature, so autofix is no; there is no code fix.
